Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `82a9a6bbdad7b753e92d22009da814e295f8d138`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/secret-field-own-ref-write.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validate-preview-parent.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/reference-forgiveness-readable-column.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/secret-field-own-ref-write.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/update-stored-row-caller-read-secret-ref-and-repoint.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx + packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts (`storedReferencesCallerReads`), packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (`servedAsStored`, `masterIdOf`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (the ADR-0113 pre-check and `previousParent`), packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts (`resolveMasterDetailParent`, `resolveMasterDetailParents`), packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts (`readUpdatePriorRow`), packages/core/src/utils/internal-write-response.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-headers-gate.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-connections.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-credentials.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-channel.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-client-secret.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/migrate-webhook-secrets.ts, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md, docs/adr/0113-required-write-contract-vs-column-constraint.md

Reviewed at 2026-11-06T23:51Z, read-only: the PR body, its file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base `bd1b7685` on `origin/main`, the check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `main`. The recogniser reads no face off the paths; the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line puts the review on the narrowing face, where the floor is every non-prose path of the diff, listed above with the two prose paths and every file the hunks make a claim about.

**Check-runs on the head as they stand.** 15 completed green, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards and Lint · PM dispatch-gates; 21 still running: Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace / source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates, Lint · ESLint / repo & tooling gates / docs & code guards / CI, release & engine gates / scoped · slot lookup & corpus / scoped · query-options erasure, and Live E2E UI; 12 skipped by their own conditions (UI-only and opt-in lanes). The queue guard reads this record together with those; nothing here is a verdict on a run that has not finished.

### ① Derived judgments

The PR narrows two accept sets of `ObjectQL.update` for a non-system caller, both by routing the comparison of a sent value against the stored row through `storedReferencesCallerReads`, the one projection PR #31031 already uses for the reference check: the stored row is kept only in the columns the caller's own read door serves exactly as stored. A system caller is returned the rows unprojected at the top of that function, so every system write is unchanged. Each change, judged:

**S1 — a `secret:` reference on a non-system update is refused, the record's own included. Right, and reached by no shipped caller.**
- Mechanism as read: `encryptSecretFields` keeps a reference only when every row the write lands on serves that same value in that column to the caller. `maskSecretFields` runs on every `find` and `findOne` with no system carve-out and turns every set `secret` column into the mask, and `servedAsStored(mask, reference)` is false, so the projection never carries a reference and the keep arm is unreachable for a non-system caller. The echoed mask is still dropped before this branch; `null` still clears; the empty string is still refused; a new value is still sealed. The refusal still names the column and never the value, and now says how to leave the field unchanged (omit it or send the mask). One answer whatever the reference names and whatever the column holds, by id and on a predicate update, matching the ADR-0112 `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 pair the row 23e of `system-context.mdx` now states.
- Consumer hunt. Every shipped `secret` column sits on five platform objects (`sys_webhook.signing_secret` / `headers_secret`, `sys_sso_provider.oidc_client_secret`, `sys_connector_connection`, `sys_connector_credential.value`, `sys_flow_credential.value`); no example app or shipped business object declares one. Each writer path, checked:
  - Console record forms (`ui/packages/components` form renderer): an object-derived `secret` maps to a password input; the row is read through the data door, so the form holds the mask and echoes it on save; the engine drops the key. No-op, as before.
  - Console settings pages (datasource, connector connections, flow-node credentials, `SettingsField`): dedicated routes, "blank keeps the stored value", a `hasSecret` flag rather than the value. None sends a reference.
  - Write responses: `maskCredentialFieldsInWriteResponse` in `@objectstack/core` masks every credential-class column on every write response, so a client that re-saves what a PATCH returned sends the mask, never a reference.
  - REST export → import (update / upsert modes): the export route reads through `engine.find` under the caller, so the file carries the mask; a re-import echoes it.
  - Webhooks: `sys_webhook` is user-writable through the generic data API and the Setup form; the headers gate lets the mask and a reference through to the engine, which answers; the form echoes the mask. The secret migration writes under a system context.
  - SSO provider: the client secret is sealed by a hook that updates under `isSystem: true`; registration is a server-only platform-admin route.
  - Connector connections, connector credentials, flow credentials: every write in `service-automation` carries `isSystem: true` (with a `userId` for attribution). Pass-through, unchanged.
  - Flows and automation: the record-change trigger serves `record` and `previous` to a flow through the ADR-0100 mask, so a flow not running as system that copies a credential column sends the mask. A flow with `runAs: 'system'` is a system write.
  - CLI: data commands go over HTTP as the API-key user (masked reads); the secret-reference union is read-only at driver level; ownership apply works below the engine.
  - MCP data tools: HTTP as the agent's user; inbound HTTP never carries the system flag; reads masked.
  - SDK: no handling of a `secret:` value anywhere in the client.
  - Seeds: the seed loader writes under a system context and compares credential columns against the mask.
  - Shipped `beforeUpdate` hooks that write the stored row back into the payload: none. The three in-tree `{ ...previous, ...data }` merges (external membership, notification template placement, the flow record decoupler) build a judged view and write nothing back; none of those objects carries a `secret` column.
  The dev's two claims hold in the tree: every in-repo secret writer uses a system context, and the masked echo is a no-op. The one in-repo reliance on the old keep was the two suites the PR rewrites. The pre-image a hook sees (`readUpdatePriorRow`, a direct driver read) does carry the stored reference, so a third-party hook that spreads `ctx.previous` onto the payload of one of those five objects is refused for a non-system caller; the changeset names it and the fix.

**S2 — a master-detail repoint pre-check binds the prior header as unresolved when the caller is not served the stored FK; the validate preview binds it the same way. Right, with one edge noted under ③.**
- Mechanism as read, by id: `namesMaster` is true exactly when the landed payload view carries the FK key (`settleMasterDetailLanding` keeps the key only when the FK lands); only then is `priorMasterIdsCallerReads` asked, one caller-context `find` by id projected to the FK. `null` (not served, hidden, transformed, or the row not returned) binds `previousParent` to `null`; in `evaluateValidationRules` a `null` `previousParent` leaves `parent` unbound for the pre-evaluation, the predicate faults, and a legacy violation cannot be proven, so the row is refused `required` — the fail-closed rule the pre-check already states ("enforcement stays on unless a legacy violation is proven"). `{ id }` reproduces the old `masterIdOf(fk, null, priorRecord)` verdict exactly, and `resolveMasterDetailParent` is now handed `{ [fk]: id }` in place of the whole pre-image, which it only ever read that one key of. A payload that does not name the FK reads nothing more and keeps `previousParent` undefined, so it defaults to `parent` as before.
- In bulk: the matched `priorRows` are projected once; the new lookup is keyed by row identity, and the consumer loop iterates the same `priorRows` array with no reassignment in between, so the identity holds. Rows bound unknown get `null`; known rows get the header from one batched elevated read, as before.
- Preview: `resolvePreviewParents` already receives stored rows projected through `servedAsStored`; it now binds `null` when the patch names the FK and the projected row lacks it, so preview and write agree for that caller. The new pin in `validate-preview-parent.test.ts` holds this with the security-shaped hide mask.
- Consumer hunt. S2 reaches a non-system caller only on an object with a parent-scoped `requiredWhen` AND a grant of `{ readable: false, editable: true }` on the master-detail FK. Every shipped `requiredWhen` (showcase invoice `issued_on`, `paid_on`; line `description`) is record-scoped — `hasParentScopedRequiredWhen` is false for all of them — and every shipped `readable: false` grant (showcase Client Liaison on project `budget`/`spent`/`budget_remaining`) is paired with `editable: false`. No shipped object, grant, form, flow, import, CLI or MCP path meets the narrowed answer. A caller who reads the FK is answered as before (control pins in both suites); a system write is answered from the rows as stored.

Tests: the four suites pin the narrowed answer on the real security plugin by id and in bulk, with the mask echo, a new value, a reading caller and a system caller as controls, and the dogfood suite pins it over REST. Nothing in the diff is prose-only; the docs row 23e matches the code.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Correct under the Post-Task Checklist rule: no metadata key, accepted value or type changes for an author, so the kind is `none` and takes `patch`; the narrowing is a non-protocol breaking change that keeps its banner and disposition. The migration prescription the body carries (omit the field or send the mask; a hook drops its `secret` columns) is the right one and is the sentence the refusal itself now gives. The `!` in the title matches.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The controlled-by-parent write gate (ADR-0055 §3) authorises a by-id detail update against the stored master even when the caller cannot read the FK column.** Separate ruling; it does not block this PR. The gate reads the stored FK to decide master EDIT access — the authorization model of its own ADR ("editing a detail requires edit access to its master"), not a comparison of a value the caller sent with the stored row. The rule this PR makes real ("an update's answer to a column the caller may write but not read must not depend on what the column holds") would, applied to the gate, amend ADR-0055 §3 itself (either deny every such write or stop judging the real master); that is an ADR amendment, a card of its own, and nothing in this diff touches `assertControlledByParentWrite`. Recorded here as a follow-up to file, not as a defect of this PR.
2. **A third-party `beforeUpdate` hook that spreads `ctx.previous` onto the payload of an object with a `secret` column is now refused for a non-system caller.** Correct and disclosed: the pre-image is a raw driver read, so such a hook writes a reference the caller never read; the changeset names the fix. No shipped hook does this.
3. **A driver that omits an unset FK from the stored row binds the prior header as unresolved for a non-system caller who names the FK, while a driver that stores `null` is judged as before.** Disclosed, direction closed, not blocking: on the omitting driver a caller who CAN read the FK, attaching a row that hangs off no master and already lacks a required value, is refused `required` instead of resting; on a null-storing driver the same caller rests under the landing header. The refusing answer is the one ADR-0113 D1 plus the pre-check's fail-closed rule actually give (a row with no prior header has no proven legacy violation), so the divergence is the null-storing driver's older rest, not a new hole; the SQL drivers store `null`. Follow-up: one verdict for both storage shapes, filed against the pre-check, not this PR.
4. **A hook that writes the stored FK back onto the payload counts as naming it on the repoint arm.** Same shape as flag 2 for the FK; the changeset names the hook case for the secret arm only. A sentence to add, not a code change.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is the published rule made real, not a capability taken away at the consumer. The published spec already says a non-system write may seal a new value or keep its own record's reference, and the read door already serves a `secret` column masked to every caller; the PR resolves "its own" to the value the caller reads, which is the only reading under which an update's answer cannot vary with a stored value the caller may not read — the invariant #31031 introduced for references and this PR extends to the two remaining sent-versus-stored comparisons on the update path. Nothing a consumer can obtain through the published surface (a data read, a write response, an export, a trigger payload) is a value the narrowed arm refuses, so no capability a published door grants is withdrawn; what is withdrawn is a keep that only a privileged read or a hook could ever have exercised. On the repoint arm, the pre-check already refused when the prior header could not be evaluated; the PR only stops a non-system caller's stored FK from supplying that header when the caller is not served it, and binds the preview the same way so `validate()` predicts the write. The one-read cost lands only on a write that names the FK on an object with a parent-scoped `requiredWhen`, or sends a reference.

Attempts to break it, all read against the cited code: a payload FK whose value the strip takes out (caller may not edit) does not name the master, so the hidden-column branch is never entered for it; a system caller is returned unprojected rows at the top of the projection and keeps both pass-throughs; a `secret` column that is also `internal` is omitted rather than masked and meets the same refusal; a row the caller's read door does not return at all (tenant scope, sharing, soft-delete) is bound unknown on the FK arm and refused on the secret arm, both the closed direction; the bulk lookup's identity keying survives because the matched array is the one iterated; the preview's stored rows were already projected, so the new `null` arm cannot admit what the write refuses. I found no path where the narrowed answer is wider than before, and none where it depends on the stored value of a column the caller is not served.

Must-fix: none.
Should-fix (follow-ups, none blocking): the webhook headers gate's docblock still describes a `secret:` reference as a value the engine leaves alone — stale for a non-system caller, a doc edit in a file outside this diff; flag 3's one-verdict-per-storage-shape follow-up on the pre-check; flag 4's sentence in the changeset; flag 1 filed as an ADR-0055 §3 card.

**VERDICT: PASS**
